item: W03/A02 recorded that the Magpie management surface was not located and that route switching and credential rotation were unverified; this locates the surface and settles what it does and does not serve

gateway.name: magpie
gateway.probe: read-only GETs plus method probes carrying an empty body and no session, against the loopback gateway the launcher already discovers; no model call, no mutation, and every probe was incapable of naming a target

error.message: name the session: ?session=<id> or the X-Magpie-Session header

withoutASession.reading: the route is per session, addressed by the session query parameter or by the X-Magpie-Session header

withAnUnknownSession.reading: an unknown session is answered rather than refused: the current route is null and carries a sequence number, so a route is a versioned per-session value

methodProbe.reading: the route path serves GET only. No write method is served, so route switching is not a management write at all - the route is an observed per-session value, and whatever sets it is the model-serving path the client already uses. Nothing was mutated, and no method on this path could have mutated anything.

notEstablished: what sets a session's route, and what the sequence number advances on
whether any other management path accepts a route write; none is advertised

quotas.shape: the live view is an object list whose entries carry a provider, a kind (subscription or balance), optional plan and windows with used/remaining/reset values, a read time and a last-served time; the history view is an object list of per-provider series whose points carry a timestamp, a remaining value, a window start and a reset time. The per-account values - an account address, plan names and balances - are deliberately not recorded here or anywhere in the evidence set
quotas.reading: the gateway exposes its own quota view and its history read-only; both are management reads, not model calls

notListedByOptions.reading: the same not_found message names the model routes only, which is what an unsupported method on a management path receives here

credentialSurface.probe: bounded read-only GET search over the plausible management names on the gateway, plus the advertised API list
credentialSurface.result: every path answered 404 with the gateway's not-found message that names the model routes, and the discovery document advertises exactly three management routes - /v1/magpie/route, /v1/magpie/quotas and /v1/magpie/quotas/history - none of which issues or rotates a credential
credentialSurface.verdictScopedToTheGateway: the gateway on this port issues and rotates no credential. That is a statement about /v1/magpie/* on 127.0.0.1:3425 and not about the product: see appManagementApi below, where the credential surface actually lives
credentialSurface.bound: a bounded negative search over plausible names and the authoritative advertised list; it does not prove that no such surface exists anywhere

appManagementApi.howFound: read-only inspection of the installed application bundle's strings, after the gateway search above showed the credential surface is not on the gateway
appManagementApi.credentialMaterial: the bundle carries caller-key prefixes sk-magpie-key- and sk-magpie-revoked-, so issuing and revoking a caller key is an operation this application offers - through its own management API rather than through the gateway
appManagementApi.addressIsConfigurable: the application's own UI text says MAGPIE_ADDR={addr} sets the gateway address, and its Settings screen carries a Gateway port field defaulting to 3425, so the port this project's launcher discovers is a setting rather than a constant

notReachableNow.probe: read-only GETs against 127.0.0.1:3430 (/api/settings, /api/providers, /api/upstream, /api/caller-keys) and a listening-socket listing for the serving process
notReachableNow.result: no connection on 3430 and the magpie process holds one listening socket only, 127.0.0.1:3425; the /api routes belong to the application's window mode and are not bound to a loopback port while it runs without its window
notReachableNow.reading: the credential surface exists in the product but is reached through the application's UI, so exercising it - like the cold start - is the user's action rather than a probe this review can make

runningInstance.reading: the instance answering on the loopback port is the installed application, not a command-line gateway, so the app path is the one in service. What remains unexercised for W03 is the cold-start transition - starting the app when it is not running - and that requires quitting a healthy application the user is using, so it is left to them.
runningInstance.discoveryWindowFlag: the discovery document reports window:true alongside the version, which is consistent with an application instance being up; it is not evidence about a cold start

notAttempted: credential rotation: no rotation route is advertised, and any such write would change a gateway the user is running
starting or restarting the management service: out of scope for a read-only discovery
recordedWithoutValues: both quota responses carry an account address and per-window values; none of those values appears in this file or anywhere in the evidence set
residual: route switching is not a management write: the gateway path serves GET only, so what remains for A02 on the routing side is observing a live session's route and the model-selection path that sets it

credential issuance and revocation exist in the application's own management API (caller keys) rather than on the gateway, and reaching them means opening the application's window, which is the user's action

the application's gateway address and port are settings (MAGPIE_ADDR, a Gateway port field defaulting to 3425), so the discovered address is a configuration this project reads rather than a constant it may assume
the contracts above were observed once against version 0.1.1109; they are point observations, not a versioned guarantee
